messages:
Jess: :wave: Hey all — I'm Jess (new on infra). I opened my first PR to fix a tiny bug + add a test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/123. Can someone give a quick orientation on our branching conventions, commit message style, and review process? CI is failing and I'm not sure what to fix. Thanks!

Sam: Welcome Jess! Quick notes: branch naming is usually `feat/<yourname>/<short-desc>` or `fix/<yourname>/<short-desc>`. Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (e.g., `feat(auth): add token refresh`). PR title should summarize like `fix(auth): correct token expiry` and use the PR template checklist. To request reviewers, add them in the GitHub reviewer UI or @mention them here. For codeowners-protected paths, reviewers are auto-requested. Ping @TJ for infra-owned files.

Reena: Also please run our pre-commit hooks & linter before pushing. We use pre-commit + black/isort/ruff. Install & run with: `pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files`. You can also run `make lint`. Example snippet from our .pre-commit-config.yaml:```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
    rev: 23.1.0
    hooks:
      - id: black
  - repo: https://github.com/charliermarsh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.12.1
    hooks:
      - id: ruff
```

TJ: Codeowners will auto-request reviewers for certain paths (e.g., `infra/**` -> @infra-team). Small bugfixes + tests usually need one approval; anything touching the serving runtime or infra stacks requires two reviewers. We prefer to squash commits before merging — use `git rebase -i` to tidy up. If your PR is WIP, set it as a draft.

ci-bot: linter failed: ruff found 3 issues

./pkg/foo.py:12:1 D100 Missing docstring
./pkg/foo.py:56:9 E225 missing whitespace around operator
./pkg/foo.py:104:5 F401 'os' imported but unused

Please run `make lint` and fix the issues.

Jess: Thanks — odd thing is I can't reproduce the ruff errors locally. `pre-commit run --all-files` is clean on my machine. CI shows the check using `python -m ruff check --select E,F`. Any hints on what might differ?

Reena: Likely a version mismatch or config difference. We pin ruff in pyproject.toml. Try `pip install ruff==0.12.1` (or the version listed in pyproject). Also confirm you have the repo config: `pyproject.toml` may define `extend-ignore` or plugin rules. If you're on Windows check CRLF issues: `git config core.autocrlf false`. If still failing paste the failing file and we can inspect.

Sam: Also verify you didn't commit generated files or files that should be ignored. Run `git status --porcelain` and `git show HEAD:pkg/foo.py` to inspect the pushed file. If you need to rewrite history to squash or fix, force-push is fine on feature branches (`git push --force-with-lease`). Reminder: we squash-and-merge on GitHub.

Maria: Welcome aboard Jess! If you'd like, I can pair-review for 15 minutes to get you unblocked. There's also an onboarding PR checklist at https://go.redwood/onboarding-prs. For new-hire PRs we usually add the `new-hire` label so reviewers know to be a bit more descriptive.

Jess: Great, thanks everyone. I pinned ruff to 0.12.1, ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and fixed the whitespace/docstring/import. Pushed a new commit and marked the PR ready, added label `new-hire` and assigned @Sam for review. Appreciate the help :pray:
